_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Industry competitive-structure analysis using Porter's Five Forces — defining industry boundaries, diagnosing each of…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "analyze this market with Porter's Five Forces"
cases.context: The agent has access to the porters-five-forces skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is porters-five-forces the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes porters-five-forces as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against prioritization, framework-fit-analysis, playing-to-win
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the porters-five-forces workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore porters-five-forces
Does not route to prioritization, framework-fit-analysis, playing-to-win when the porters-five-forces scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
